items.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

items.title: MLA: kv_b_proj.weight.dtype AttributeError on quantized ColumnParallelLinear in chunked prefill
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Description

When using a quantized (AWQ/GPTQ/compressed-tensors) model with MLA attention, vLLM crashes with an `AttributeError` during chunked prefill because `kv_b_proj` is a `ColumnParallelLinear` that lacks a `.weight` attribute after quantization.

## Error

```
AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

at `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:2094` in `_compute_prefill_context`:

```python
kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype)
```

## Root Cause

Lines 2084-2087 already correctly handle quantized layers:

```python
_kv_b_proj_w_dtype = (
    self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype
    if hasattr(self.kv_b_proj, "weight")
    else self.kv_b_proj.params_dtype
)
```

But line 2094 ignores `_kv_b_proj_w_dtype` and directly accesses `self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype` without the `hasattr` guard.

## Fix

On line 2094, replace:

```python
kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype)
```

with:

```python
kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(_kv_b_proj_w_dtype)
```

The variable `_kv_b_proj_w_dtype` is already computed with the correct `hasattr` guard immediately above.

## Impact

vLLM EngineCore crashes with a fatal error, forcing a full restart (service enters crash loop under load). All inflight requests fail with HTTP 500.

## Environment

- vLLM version: v0.21.1rc1.dev384 (nightly, also present in current main)
- Model: GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit (quantized with compressed-tensors)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3090 (CUDA 12.9)
- Quantization: compressed-tensors (AWQ group_size=32, num_bits=4)
- CUDA graphs: enabled
- MLA: enabled (model uses Multi-head Latent Attention)

## Stack Trace

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 2094, in _compute_prefill_context
    kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype)
                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

items.title: [RFC]: KVPP (KV pipeline parallel, LayerSplit) for vLLM
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

This proposal is inspired by **Section 4, “LayerSplit,”** of Z.ai's [*Scaling Pain of Coding Agent Serving: Lessons from Debugging GLM-5 at Scale*](https://z.ai/blog/scaling-pain). LayerSplit introduces layer-wise ownership of KV-cache storage and makes the cache available to the other ranks when a layer runs. This RFC describes how to express that idea in vLLM's KV-cache planning and model-execution lifecycle.

An experimental implementation already exists in [vllm-ascend's KVPP design](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/main/developer_guide/Design_Documents/kvpp/) and [feature guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/main/user_guide/feature_guide/kvpp/).

### Terminology: why “KV-PP”

The existing implementation calls this feature **KVPP**, short for **KV pipeline parallel**. We propose writing the same name as **KV-PP** when explaining the parallelism axis. If vLLM's Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) is viewed, at the KV-storage level, as **KV-CP**—partitioning a sequence's KV tokens across ranks—then KV-PP is the complementary **layer-axis** partition: ranks persist different layers' KV caches and obtain a complete layer before using it.

| Conceptual axis | Persistent KV ownership | Access during attention |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KV-CP analogy (DCP) | Different token or context portions of a layer | Distributed attention uses the rank-local context and combines results. |
| KV-PP (this RFC) | Different complete layers | The layer owner makes its cache available to all computing ranks before cache access. |

### Goals

- Increase the logical cache-block capacity when replicated, persistent KV storage is the limiting resource.
- Keep scheduler block IDs, prefix-cache semantics, and request admission based on one complete logical KV-cache specification.
- Allow a device backend to choose layer owners, physical layouts, and a collective transport without teaching the scheduler about those details.

items.bodyExcerpt:

- vLLM source commit `385dce36bcee42309924a5ece951a96db3dce7f2`, in image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:b0501f99fec5136f248f78d5850977a2ec32d55cd9a665f4a9ffef24cbdf7fe5`, with local patches unrelated to the indexer's key path. The same code is on `main` at `36f94d5fe8a3` (2026-09-24).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04.3 (aarch64).
- 2 × NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark class), TP=2 over RoCE, driver 580.173.02.
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (and a requantized derivative), MTP depth 3, `--enforce-eager`, temperature 0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The kpool sparse indexer in `vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py` is replicated on every TP rank: `wq_b` is a `ReplicatedLinear` and `wk_weights_proj` uses `disable_tp=True`, so each rank computes the same keys and candidate sets from the same inputs. That only works if the ranks compute them **bit-identically**. Nothing enforces this, and one step in the key path does not guarantee it.

The key is normalised by `_fused_indexer_k_norm(kw[:, :head_dim], ...)`, a leaf compiled with `torch.compile(dynamic=True)`. Inductor turns it into a persistent reduction with three candidate configs (`XBLOCK` 1, 8 and 32, `num_warps` 2), and each rank picks one by benchmarking the first time it runs. `XBLOCK=1` computes the row reduction in a different order: on a fixed strided input of 2,048 × 160 → `[:, :128]`, its output differs from `XBLOCK` 8 and 32 in 2 of 2,048 rows (8 and 32 agree; the same classes on both GPUs). The difference is small, but the indexer then selects the top 512 of 540 pools per row. Where pools are close to a tie, a slightly different key selects a different set on one rank. The two ranks' attention outputs then differ, the all-reduce mixes them, and the greedy completion forks.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] DSv3.2: fuse indexer Q-RoPE+quant + K-norm/RoPE/quant/cache
items.bodyExcerpt:
Port [ROCm/ATOM#788](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/788)'s indexer fused-kernel shape into vLLM. Replaces the `k_norm → rotary_emb → per_token_group_quant_fp8 → cache` chain (and the Q-side `per_token_group_quant_fp8`) inside `Indexer.forward` with a single AITER kernel `aiter.indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` (ROCm/aiter#3185, correctness fixes in ROCm/aiter#3451).

> **Companion:** ROCm/aiter#3451 — required. Without it GSM8K strict-match drops 0.95 → 0.49.

## Gating

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV32_INDEXER_FUSION` (default off) + main AITER toggle; auto-disabled when the running AITER build does not expose `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`. The kernel hard-asserts `index_head_dim == 128`, `qk_rope_head_dim == 64`, `head_dim == quant_block_size`; `Indexer.__init__` only enables the path if all three hold and `model_type != "glm_moe_dsa"`.

## Design notes

- **Stays inside the existing custom op.** Calling the fused kernel from inside `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` keeps `q_fp8` and `weights_out` from escaping — an earlier version that registered them as a separate op leaked pointers across piecewise-cudagraph segments and tanked GSM8K to ~1%.
- **Persistent workspace** for `q_fp8` / `weights_out`, grown monotonically. Otherwise 61 indexer layers × 2 allocations per decode step churn the eager allocator.
- **K stride fixup.** The kernel asserts `k.stride(0) == head_dim`, but the upstream `.contiguous()` is a no-op on `size(0) == 1` views. We rewrite the metadata via `as_strided` when it's safe, else `empty + copy_`.
- **`preshuffle=True`.** Downstream consumers read MFMA 16×16 SHUFFLE; the original call site passed `False` and silently produced garbage. Bytewise-equal to the unfused triton write after the fix.
- **fp32 LN params** passed through as-is (required by ROCm/aiter#3451).

## Purpose

`Glm4MoeMTP` is not decorated with `@support_torch_compile`. As a result, the MTP draft forward executes as eager Python and misses every Inductor fusion pass that the target forward enjoys - most notably the AITER allreduce + RMSNorm fusion, RMSNorm + quant fusion, and silu+mul+fp8-quant fusion.

Adding the decorator brings MTP behaviour in line with the canonical `DeepSeekMTP` pattern (`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py`, L185) and makes the draft eligible for the same compile-time fusions as the target.

items.bodyExcerpt:
This PR is the reasoning half of Hunyuan V3 support in the Rust frontend. The `hy_v3` tool parser landed in #43872, but the reasoning parser was missing, so reasoning output from a Hy3 model isn't split out. Roadmap item is `hy_v3` under #44280.

Hy3 uses standard `<think>` / `</think>` tags, so this registers `hy_v3` as the eighth `Qwen3ReasoningParser` alias, next to DeepSeek V3/V4, GLM45, Kimi K2, MiniMax M2, Nemotron V3, and Step3, plus `hy3` / `hy_v3` model patterns mirroring the tool side. No new parser code. The Python parser's two hy_v3-specific behaviors are covered by the prompt-first design: the Hy3 template always leaves a reasoning boundary at the end of the generation prompt (`<think></think>` for no_think, `<think>` for low/high), so prompt-boundary initialization already lands in the right state, and `token_suffix` is only non-empty on the opensource checkpoint, not the preview one vLLM tests against; a suffixed checkpoint fails parser creation loudly rather than misparsing.

I also added a roundtrip fixture over the real `tencent/Hy3-preview` template (public, ungated), covering the no_think default path end to end. The thinking path can't roundtrip on this template at all since history rendering strips reasoning, same reason gemma4/kimi_k25 are restricted, and the extraction state machine is already covered by the qwen3/glm45/deepseek_v4 roundtrips sharing the same parser. `tool_call_mix` needs harness work due to per-turn eos differences, so I left it out on purpose. ## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.

- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.
This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel.

This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty`
and the fill is removed.

## Safety

The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside
`[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial
load, so padding values are never read. The top-k result is unchanged.

| FP32 fill GPU time | 1,250.2 ms | **0 ms** |

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Terminate streamed tool arguments the flush cannot extend
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A streaming tool call can end with `finish_reason` set while `arguments` is cut off mid-string. Any client that calls `json.loads` on the accumulated arguments fails on it. Reproduced live on Qwen3.8-27B in 7 of 25 requests sent straight at the worker, no proxy in the path.

`_safe_arg_prefix` (`parser_engine.py:283`) deliberately streams unterminated string values for prefix-stable keys. Its own docstring carries the contract: "String values for keys in `string_keys` are prefix-stable, so stream their unterminated content instead of buffering long arguments until the closing tag arrives." Something has to close them, and that something is the flush.

`_flush_arg_converter` (`parser_engine.py:963`) re-derives the arguments with `partial=False`. Every in-tree `arg_converter` builds its result from completed parameters and folds the still-open one in under `if partial:`. So when generation ends while a parameter is open, the non-partial re-derivation **drops that parameter**, and the result is neither longer than nor a prefix of what was already streamed. Both guards fail, the function returns `None`, and nothing ever terminates the prefix the client is holding.

This is not conditional on the model misbehaving. Anything that ends generation with a parameter open reaches it: a `max_tokens` stop, a stop string, or a malformed continuation.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Two fixes to the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` backend that are prerequisites for serving NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) with the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM120/SM121 devices such as the NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10). Related to #45317 (DSA models unable to serve on GB10).

Note on scope: the GLM-5.3-Flash model architecture itself is not upstream yet, so no in-tree model exercises these paths today with `qk_rope_head_dim=0`. These are the attention-layer fixes we needed on top of a Glm5Next-enabled build; submitting them separately so the backend is ready when the model lands, and so other GB10 users patching locally have a reference. Happy to convert to draft or fold into a larger enablement PR if maintainers prefer.

**Fix 1: NoPE models crash in `concat_and_cache_mla` (fp8_ds_mla layout assumes a rope section)**

The `fp8_ds_mla` KV-cache tile is a fixed 656-byte DeepSeek-shaped layout (512-dim fp8 latent + scales + 64-dim bf16 rope), and the compiled `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel asserts `pe_dim == 64`. Models with `qk_rope_head_dim=0` crash on that assert. This PR zero-pads the missing rope section symmetrically on both the KV-write and the query side.

Bit-exactness argument: a zero rope vector contributes exactly 0 to the `q_pe · k_pe` dot product, so attention scores are bit-for-bit identical to true NoPE. This is a layout adaptation, not a numerical approximation.

**Fix 2: support check validates raw `index_topk` instead of the effective buffer width**

The SM120 support check requires `index_topk == 2048` (the only width the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA kernel is instantiated for). However, what actually reaches the kernel is the topk *buffer* width: the indexer emits `index_topk` plus up to `index_kpool - 1` always-selected tail tokens, padded up to a multiple of 128. ## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As

processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache

## Purpose

`speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` is unusable with the generic MTP
drafter: enabling it does not fall back to a slower path, it fails engine startup.

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekMTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

The reduction itself already lives in core as `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` — each
TP rank argmaxes its own vocab shard and only `(value, index)` pairs are gathered. Both
opt-in sites probe the draft model for the method and raise without it:

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` (V2 model runner)
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`

`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py` has `compute_logits` but no

is the `deepseek_v3` family — DeepSeek-V3 and R1 — on every platform:

| checkpoint `model_type` | architecture | resolved draft class | platform |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | `DeepSeekMTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | all |

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank. 
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`

Building on top of @almogtavor 's work https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include, 
 - SlidingWindowMLASpec
 - Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
 models. 
 
Notably, 
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 
- zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category. 

### Changes:
 - in the replicated_layout check, 
   * Unwrap `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` and check that the internal layer specs are MLA
   * Check if all the layer_spec in all the Attention groups are in [MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec]
   * Additionally, check that the advertises `num_kv_heads = 1`, indicating TP sharding of KV heads is not possible. 
   * Remove the existing size check 
   ```
        and worker_kv_bytes_per_block
        == single_group_spec.page_size_bytes
        * len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[0].layer_names)
   ```
    this is critical and loosens the existing conditions on `main` . This is because the KV cache groups are flattened in the Scheduler process here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/038cb14bd7874030e98bb6edc4b6f4efe649fff7/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L2376 . 
    Specifically, the realization of the comment, 
    ```
            # All layers in the UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs have the same type,
            # so use an arbitrary one to initialize the scheduler.
    ```

items.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM90 sparse MLA IMA on >16k-row steps by chunking plan/run
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a CUDA illegal-memory-access crash whenever a single scheduled step packs more than 16384 query rows on the SM90 sparse MLA backend (the GLM-5.3-Flash default), e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` with a 28k-token prefill chunk, or 32k tokens scheduled across concurrent requests.

**Root cause (flashinfer 0.6.18.post1, the pinned version).** The SM90 batch-MLA plan hardcodes `max_total_num_works = 16384` and never checks it: the load-balancing schedule is `std::copy`'d into per-array regions sized for 16384 works, so a larger step silently overwrites neighboring schedule arrays, and the kernel then reads garbage `q_indptr`/`kv_indptr` (IMA in `BatchMLAPageAttentionHopper`). This backend feeds one varlen row per query token, so any step with more than 16384 scheduled tokens overflows. flashinfer 0.7.0 raised the limit to 65536 and added a hard error, but vLLM pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`. Small overflows (e.g. 16385 works) do not even fault — they run with a corrupted schedule.

**Fix.** When a step has more than `_MAX_PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS = 8192` query rows, plan and run the MQA as independent row chunks: the builder plans each chunk into its own `_SM90State` (a lazily grown pool), and `forward_mqa` runs each state's row range and concatenates. Each row is already an independent varlen query (causality is encoded in the top-k selection, `causal=False`), so chunking is exact. The bound is 8192 rather than 16384 so the work count stays provably under 16384 even with split-kv rows: works <= rows + total_kv_len / kv_len_limit, and `kv_len_limit` tracks total_kv_len / num_clusters. Steps at or under the limit keep the existing single-plan path unchanged, including CUDA-graph replay.

## Not a duplicate

- #56969 fixed a different OOB in this backend (mixed prefill/decode batches); it is in the tested tree and the crash still reproduces without this change.
- #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and the indexer prefill workspace sizing; different call sites.

## Purpose

`BlockTable.commit_block_table()` in the V1 model runner re-uploads the whole
active `[num_reqs, max_num_blocks_per_req]` block table host→device on every
step, for every KV-cache group, even when no row changed since the last upload.

A row only changes when a request is admitted, moved, removed, or crosses a
KV-block boundary. This PR tracks a conservative interval of rows changed since
the last commit that covered them and skips the copy when that interval lies
outside `[0, num_reqs)`. When it does copy, it is the same single contiguous
bulk transfer as today.

items.title: [Bugfix] Stop allocator fragmentation from shrinking the KV cache during memory profiling
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Wrap the memory-profiling forward pass in `Worker._scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20)`, the same scoped allocator setting #41268 applies around weight loading.

During `profile_run`, workspaces such as the MoE workspace grow in steps, and each step frees the previous, smaller buffer. With PyTorch's default (unlimited) `max_split_size_mb`, a later small allocation can be carved out of one of those freed multi-GiB blocks. That live block keeps the whole segment reserved through the `empty_cache()` in `memory_profiling`. The profiler measures consumption from free device memory, so the stranded segment is counted as consumed and taken out of the KV cache.

How much gets stranded depends on allocation order, so it varies per rank. With context parallelism the worst rank in each group sets the group's KV size, so the loss compounds. With a split limit, blocks above the limit are never split, so they stay whole and `empty_cache()` releases them. The limit is restored when the profiling pass exits, before `memory_profiling` measures, so serving and KV cache allocation run with the original allocator settings.

`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` also avoids the stranding. But vLLM rejects it alongside a KV connector such as NIXL unless `--enable-cumem-allocator` is also set, and in the deployment below that combination raised baseline consumption by ~2.9 GiB on every GPU. The scoped split limit keeps the default `cudaMalloc` allocator throughout.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py::test_scoped_max_split_keeps_freed_large_blocks_releasable` (needs CUDA). It frees a 512 MiB buffer and then allocates a 2 MiB tensor. Without the scope, the tensor pins the 512 MiB segment through `empty_cache()`. Inside `_scoped_allocator_max_split(20)`, the segment is released.

## Purpose

Kimi K2.5/K3 passes contiguous `[patches, 3, 14, 14]` inputs to its shared vision tower. Each Conv2d call produces one output per patch, so use the existing `Conv2dLayer.forward_native` GEMM path. ## Purpose

`AnthropicMessagesRequest` never declared a `thinking` field, so `/v1/messages` silently dropped the documented Anthropic parameter (Pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`). Clients asking for disabled thinking or a token budget got whatever `output_config.effort` implied.

items.title: [Core] Add --release-weight-page-cache to drop checkpoint pages after load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Adds `--release-weight-page-cache` (`LoadConfig.release_weight_page_cache`, default off). With the flag on, each worker calls `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` on every checkpoint file once its own `model.load_weights` has returned.

The checkpoint is read exactly once. On hosts that keep a large CPU KV tier in shm next to the weights, the clean checkpoint pages left in the page cache after loading (about 700 GiB for a 355B MoE at bf16) hold the node at its memory edge for the life of the pod, and every later start on the same node begins at that edge. Direct reclaim there contends on `mmap_lock` with the worker's per-step `mmap`/`munmap` traffic (CPython 3.12 frame data-stack chunks inside every MoE layer, python/cpython#142183), so a DP step can stall until the collective times out. Releasing the pages after load removes that trigger.

The pages are clean and unmapped by the time the release runs, so they are freed immediately. A rank still reading a file another rank already released re-reads it from disk, bounded by the seconds of skew between ranks, which is why the flag is opt-in. The cost is a cold re-read on the next start of the same node.

## Test Plan

GLM-5.3 prefill, DEP32 (8 workers per pod), 4 pods per group, on a vLLM 0.29-based image with the same pod templates as the serving deployment: the release logic run as a post-load step, then an in-place restart of the group, then two cache-churn soaks (160 sessions x 2 rounds, 32 concurrent, 66K-token prompts) and 16 x 157K-token prompts at concurrency 8.

## Test Result

- 703 GiB released per node in 13-16 s; MemFree 550-650 -> 770-855 GiB; shm tier untouched.
- Serving unchanged: TTFT medians 32.2 s / 5.4 s (rounds 1/2) and 50.6 s / 50.4 s on the long prompts, equal or better than the same runs without the release; 0 errors.
- Cold and warm loads both 200-260 s, so nothing measurable is lost on the next start.
- After the restart the nodes came up with 547-652 GiB free instead of 6-33 GiB

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix index_kpool handling in FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## 1. Root cause

The FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA builder incorrectly used the main MLA cache's
`tokens_per_state` as the sparse indexer's `index_kpool`. These values describe
different layouts: GLM-5.3-Flash stores one main MLA cache state per token
(`tokens_per_state=1`), while its sparse indexer pools every four tokens
(`index_kpool=4`).

For example, with `index_topk=2048` and a context length of 2051, the indexer
produces 2048 selected token slots plus three tokens from the incomplete trailing
pool. The correct valid length is:

```text
2048 + 2051 % 4 = 2051
```

The old code instead calculated:

```text
2048 + 2051 % 1 = 2048
```

The three trailing slots were generated correctly but excluded from the length
passed to FlashInfer, so the kernel did not attend to them. Once the context
exceeds 2048, this can omit one to three recent tokens on three out of every four
decoding steps.

GSM8K did not expose the issue because every evaluated request stayed below 2048
tokens. In GPQA, it repeatedly trigges the incorrect length calculation.

## 2. Fix

Read `index_kpool` from the model configuration. Models without an `index_kpool`
value fall back to `1`, representing no pooling:

```python
index_kpool = getattr(hf_config, "index_kpool", None)
self._index_kpool = 1 if index_kpool is None else int(index_kpool)
```

## 3. Test results

All evaluations used GLM-5.3-Flash native FP8 weights, BF16 KV cache, TP8, no
speculative decoding, on H200.
